record.paper_title: Recent Results and Open Problems on the Hydrodynamics of Disordered Asymmetric Exclusion and Zero-Range Processes
record.context_brief: Phase transition and flux shape for disordered TASEP/K-exclusion
record.original_question: For the disordered totally asymmetric simple exclusion process, and more generally the one-dimensional totally asymmetric K-exclusion process with site disorder where each site can hold at most K particles and the macroscopic limit has an unknown concave flux function f_K on [0,K], determine whether the model exhibits a phase transition analogous to the disordered zero-range process. A specific open question is whether the flux function f_K(rho) contains a flat segment on an interval centered around rho = K/2.

evidence.quote: Problem 4. For the disordered TASEP, any new rigorous results would be welcome. For example, is there a phase transition similar to the one for disordered ZRP? Does the flux function fK(ρ) have a flat segment on an interval around ρ = K/2?

The disordered SEP is less well understood than the ZRP. The reason is that no invariant distributions have been found. Presently we can prove the existence of a hydrodynamic limit for the totally asymmetric SEP, in dimension one. But the flux function f of the macroscopic equation (2.18) remains unknown. The theorem covers a more general totally asymmetric SEP, namely the so-called K-exclusion, where each site admits K particles instead of just one.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional totally asymmetric K-exclusion process with quenched site disorder, defined as follows. Fix an integer K ≥ 1. The state space is {0,1,…,K}^Z, where η(x) ∈ {0,…,K} denotes the number of particles at site x. To each site x ∈ Z is attached an independent random rate α(x), drawn from a common distribution supported in (0,∞) with infimum c ≥ 0 (the disorder is assumed to satisfy standard ergodicity/stationarity conditions). Given a configuration η, a particle jumps from site x to site x+1 at rate α(x) provided η(x) ≥ 1 and η(x+1) ≤ K−1 (the case K = 1 is the disordered TASEP). 

Under hyperbolic rescaling, this process admits a hydrodynamic limit governed by a scalar conservation law ∂_t ρ + ∂_x f_K(ρ) = 0, where f_K : [0,K] → [0,∞) is a concave macroscopic flux function with f_K(0) = f_K(K) = 0.

(a) Does this disordered K-exclusion process exhibit a phase transition analogous to that proved for the disordered nearest-neighbor asymmetric zero-range process — namely, the existence of a critical density above which the system fails to reach equilibrium and instead develops a condensation/plateau phenomenon?

(b) Equivalently in the macroscopic picture, does the flux function f_K(ρ) contain a flat segment on a non-degenerate interval centered around ρ = K/2?
artifact.status_search_result: For K = 1 (disordered TASEP), Bahadoran and Bodineau (Electron. J. Probab. 2018, "Quantitative estimates for the flux of TASEP with dilute site disorder") proved the existence of a flat plateau in the flux function f under a sufficiently dilute site-disorder assumption (e.g. a slow power-tail of the disorder distribution near its minimum), confirming a phase-transition signature analogous to the disordered ZRP. The full conjecture — that the plateau exists for general disorder distributions and that it is centered around ρ = 1/2 (and more generally around ρ = K/2 for the K-exclusion case with K ≥ 2) — remains open. Related work (Bahadoran–Bodineau, Braz. J. Probab. Stat. 2015) gives properties and conjectures supporting this picture.

status_evidence.title: Quantitative estimates for the flux of TASEP with dilute site disorder
status_evidence.snippet: The flux function of the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process with site disorder exhibits a flat segment for sufficiently dilute disorder, under a decay assumption of the maximum current implied by a slow power tail near the minimum.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of a plateau in the disordered TASEP flux is proved under dilution/slow-tail assumptions, partially resolving the question for K=1.

status_evidence.title: Properties and conjectures for the flux of TASEP with site disorder
status_evidence.snippet: Properties and conjectures for the flux of TASEP with site disorder.
status_evidence.claim: General properties and conjectures regarding the plateau in f are formulated; full statement remains conjectural.

status_evidence.title: Existence of a plateau for the flux of TASEP with site disorder (HAL)
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of a plateau for the flux of TASEP with site disorder.
status_evidence.claim: Plateau established under additional assumptions on disorder.
